To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Coppa Nevicata archaeological site was located in a coastal lagoon that gradually became isolated and ultimately transformed into terrestrial environment.
the Coppa Nevigate archaeological site was situated on the eastern shore of a broad lagoonal environment which was gradually transformed into a terrestrial landscape.

(1) the lagoon was in a semi-closed state for 2.6 kyr and then closed, (2) a hiatus in deposition occurred from the Late Roman Period to the Middle Ages, (3) the lagoon opened around 400 cal. yrs BP, and (4) the lagoon became dry and was transformed into an open grassland.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the environmental changes that affected the Tavolière Plain during the Holocene, and their possible influence on the development and evolution of the Coppa Nevigate settlement, and more generally of the ancient human occupation in the Tavolière Plain.
reconstructing the Holocene environmental history of the Tavoliera Plain, a large coastal area that has been inhabited since the Early Neolithic.
the environmental history of a region that has undergone a series of changes in response to natural processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lagoon and the surrounding environment were not affected by the human activities, but the human presence in the area was probably influenced by the environmental evolution.
the Coppa Nevigate settlement was situated on the fringe of a lagoon that was gradually isolated from the sea.
the Coppa Nevicata site was situated on the shore of a semi-closed brackish lagoon, which was gradually reduced in size and transformed into a freshwater environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Holocene evolution of the lagoonal environment was mainly controlled by the sea level changes and the related hydrological conditions.

the Coppa Nevigate settlement was located at the edge of a lagoon that underwent a natural process of isolation and drying, and that the Coppa Neigate people were not responsible for the progressive disappearance of the lagoon.
the lagoon was formed during a sea-level rise and was subsequently transformed into a closed water body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental changes that occurred in the Palude-Frattarolo–lago Salso area are in line with the general pattern of environmental changes in the Tavolière Plain and the central Mediterranean.
the environmental history of the Tavoliero Plain is characterised by a long period of stability and a more recent period of instability.
